editorial.headline: Analog Television Broadcasting: Nationally Open, Address-Specific in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Analog television broadcasting is open to foreign ownership nationally, while Bali does not block it under its moratorium but requires address-level verification.
editorial.body:
For analog television broadcasting and programming, the national position is clear: foreign ownership may reach 100%. In Bali, the activity is not blocked by the province-wide PMA moratorium. Its medium-high/high-risk position nevertheless makes address-level verification part of the practical picture.

This activity covers the operation of television broadcasting and programming services using analogue signals. It encompasses work carried out through a television broadcasting studio and the facilities used to transmit video to the public, affiliates, and/or subscribers. Those transmissions may travel through terrestrial networks, cable, or satellite. The emphasis is on the broadcasting operation itself: a service that brings scheduled television programming from studio and transmission infrastructure to its intended audience.

The record leaves the activity open across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That breadth matters because the classification does not confine analogue television broadcasting to a single size of operator. A business registering this activity may therefore sit at any of those scales, while the national PMA position permits foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling of 100%.

Bali requires a more precise reading, not a more pessimistic one. The provincial moratorium permanently blocks PMA registration for low- and medium-low-risk activities across the island, but this record is marked medium-high/high risk and is expressly not blocked by that moratorium. The remaining instruction is practical rather than prohibitive: verify the position for the specific address. For a founder assessing Bali, that distinction is the essential one—this is not an activity shut out by the moratorium, yet its local treatment should be checked where the operation will be based.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, analogue television broadcasting is not shut out by the moratorium, but its position should be verified for the specific address.
